    Lemma 2.1: normed bases from the basic algebra #

    lem:nonbasic-basis. Let B₀ = eAe with AeA = A have a normed multiplicative basis with primitive idempotents e_i. "Every basis element b belongs to one corner: in b = Σ e_i b e_j, each nonzero summand is a basis element by multiplicativity […]." Each primitive idempotent f of a complete set of A has fA ≅ e_i A, given by elements u ∈ fAe_i, v ∈ e_iAf with uv = f, vu = e_i (here from 1 ∈ AeA and the local corner fAf). "For each element b ∈ e_iB₀e_j of the given basis, take all its single-entry matrices E_{iα,jβ}(b)": here u_s b v_t. "Their multiplication is E_{iα,jβ}(b) E_{lγ,mδ}(c) = E_{iα,mδ}(bc) if (j,β) = (l,γ), 0 otherwise […]. The single-entry matrices E_{iα,iα}(e_i) form a complete set of primitive orthogonal idempotents. The radical powers of A have the same block description with e_i (rad B₀)^n e_j in each block."

    References #

    • Multiplicative bases and deformations of representation-finite algebras, https://github.com/haruhisa-enomoto/multiplicative-bases-deformations. Numbered statements cited here refer to it.
